rulings.Case Title: DEON V BRIMMER VS. CITY & COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: DEMURRER to PETITION FOR WRIT OF MANDATE/ PROHIBITION/ CERTIFICATION
rulings.Rulings: On the Law and Motion/Discovery calendar for September 15, 2026, line 1. RESPONDENTS SAN FRANCISCO HUMAN SERVICE AGENCY, CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO'S DEMURRER TO PETITION FOR WRIT OF MANDATE. Respondents City and County of San Francisco and San Francisco Human Service Agency's demurrer to the petition for writ of mandate filed by petitioner Dion Brimmer is sustained with leave to file a first amended petition no later than October 14, 2026 if, in good faith, he can allege facts showing that he can one or more viable claims against the respondents. Brimmer's petition seeks a writ of mandate that is contrary to California law. In the introduction of his writ Brimmer writes that he seeks a writ of mandate compelling respondents to "increase CAAP/SSIP/GA grant levels to no less than $4,200.00 per month, the minimum amount required to meet basic needs under Welfare & Institutions Code ss. 17000-17001." The major flaw in the petition is that respondents' obligations per the cited code sections is not measured by "a standard of aid that meets the actual basic needs of its indigent general assistance recipients, but [respondents] may provide a lower level of benefits, provided that standard of aid meets the 62 percent [of a guideline based on the 1991 federal official poverty line] requirement." (Cleary v. County of Alameda (2011) 196 Cal. App. 4th 826, 840, quoting Bell v. Board of Supervisors (1994) 23 Cal. App. 4th 1695, 1704 relying on Welfare & Institutions Code 17000.5)). Thus, per the very statutes that Brimmer cites, he is not entitled to a grant that meets his basic needs. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. DEFENDANTS COOKIES CREATIVE CONSULTING & PROMOTIONS, LLC, COOKIES CREATIVE CONSULTING & PROMOTIONS, INC., COOKIES SF, LLC, COOKIES CREATIVE PT, LLC, COOKIES CREATIVE PRODUCTIONS & CONSULTING, INC., BIGGERBIZZ, LLC, LEMONNADE, INC., PARKER BERLING, IAN HABENICHT, GILBERT MILAM JR., CRYSTAL MILLICAN, LESJAI CHANG'S Motion to Compel Further Post Judgment Discovery Responses by Judgment Debtor Cookies Retail, LLC. Judgment creditor Cookies Creative Consulting & Promotions, LLC's motion to compel further post-judgment discovery responses by judgment debtor Cookies Retail, LLC is granted. No later than October 6, 2026 CRE must serve verified code-compliant responses without objections other than privilege objections to CCCP's second post-judgment interrogatories 36-67 and second post-judgment requests for production 36-72 and produce all responsive documents. Any responsive information or documents claimed to be privileged must be identified in a privilege log. CRE has a legitimate interest in not having to respond to judgment enforcement discovery from both CCCP and Baker & McKenzie LLP. Because CCCP and Baker are working together as to this discovery and their judgment collection interests are aligned, CRE is not at risk of having to respond to judgment enforcement discovery from both CCCP and Baker. Due to this lack of risk and CCP CCCP is permitted by CCP 368.5 to remain as a named party, CRE's standing objections to substantively responding to the second post-judgment sets of discovery requests lack merit and are overruled. CRE has not shown that any of its other objections have merit, so those objections are also overruled. rulings.Case Title: JESSICA DELANIA HUISA ORTIZ VS. UBER TECHNOLOGIES, INC. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Defendant Ahmad Jawid Bonyadi To Appear For Deposition; Request For Monetary Sanctions; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities; Declaration Of Michael P. Green
rulings.Rulings: On the Law and Motion/Discovery calendar for September 15, 2026, line 3. PLAINTIFF JESSICA HUISA ORTIZ'S Motion to Compel Defendant Ahmad Jawid Bonyadi to Appear for Deposition; Request for Monetary Sanctions. Plaintiff Jessica Ortiz's motion to compel deposition of defendant Ahmad Bonyadi and for monetary sanctions is granted. Unless the parties agree to a different date, Bonyadi must make himself available for deposition no earlier than October 1, 2026 and no later than October 31, 2026 whether or not the Dashcam footage has been received by his counsel as of the date of the deposition. If the parties cannot agree on a date for the deposition, no later than September 18, 2026 counsel for Bonyadi must provide three available dates in October 2026 and no later than September 21, 2026 counsel for Ortiz may select which of those days the deposition will take place. Ortiz must provide a Dari interpreter for the deposition unless Bonyardi's counsel advises Ortiz's counsel in writing that a Dari interpreter is not needed. No later than October 31, 2026 Bonyadi and his counsel must pay Ortiz $2,000 in reasonable monetary sanctions, calculated at 5 hours at a reasonable hourly rate of $400. Ortiz is entitled to take Bonyardi's deposition and Bonyardi has not provided a persuasive reason why the deposition should be deferred until his counsel receives the Dashcam footage. Ortiz acted in part with substantial justification and in part without substantial justification. Ortiz acted with substantial justification in her position that Bonyardi should not be able to delay his deposition after he agreed to a date for the deposition, but acted without substantial justification by not cancelling the court reporter, interpreter and videographer once Bonyardi made it clear that he would not attend the July 30 deposition. Bonyardi acted without substantial justification by not attending the July 30 deposition. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person.
